title: Ampleness on the saturation of an affine open under a connected smooth group
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and let $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type with geometrically connected fibres (for every field $\Omega$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ the fibre $H_\Omega=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is connected) [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A group scheme is equipped with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, with an $H$-action $a:H\times_SZ\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every affine open subscheme $U\subseteq Z$, the image $W=a(H\times_SU)\subseteq Z$ on underlying points is open. Give $W$ its open subscheme structure. Then $W$ admits an ample invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module in the absolute sense of [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No homogeneity of $Z$, affineness of $H$, commutativity, or relative dimension bound is assumed; empty $U$ is allowed.

source.place: Proposition quoted in the proof of 4.2.2, printed p.57, attributed there to Raynaud, Faisceaux amples, V.3.10 (OCR V.5.10). Specialize its quasi-affine open to an affine open and its normal locally Noetherian base to an affine normal Noetherian domain. The quoted conclusion constructs a relatively ample boundary-divisor line on the saturation; over an affine base it is ample in the absolute sense. Local archive WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: The map $T:H\times_SZ\to H\times_SZ$, $(h,z)\mapsto(h,hz)$, is an isomorphism with inverse $(h,z)\mapsto(h,h^{-1}z)$, by the action identities. The projection to $Z$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2); hence $a=\operatorname{pr}_2\circ T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c). By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] it is flat and locally of finite presentation. On affine source and target charts its ring maps are flat of finite presentation, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-finite-presentation-open] says their maps are open. Taking their union shows $a$ is open. Since $H\times_SU$ is open, its image $W$ is open. The identity gives $U\subseteq W$. Associativity and inverses give $H\cdot W=W$: a point represented after a residue-field extension by $hu$ is sent to $(gh)u$, and every point of $W$ occurs by the identity. Thus the action factors through $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and the action identities restrict to it.

source.place: Tags 01UA (lemma-fppf-open), 056G (lemma-smooth-open); group-action factorization as in BLR 6.6 Theorem 2

proof.text: The single affine chart $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ makes $S$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and affine schemes are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its local rings $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $Z$ and $H$ are Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so is $W$. The open immersion $W\to Z$ is of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation]. Smoothness restricts to $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Both $W\to S$ and $H\to S$ are separated: the restricted diagonal is the base change of the original diagonal, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). They are quasi-compact since their sources are Noetherian, and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Their local finite presentation follows from [lem-pc-smooth-flat], hence they are of finite presentation; in particular $W\to S$ is of finite type.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01OV; normal affine base and finite presentation setup

proof.text: We check that $U_t$ is dense in $W_t$ for every $t\in S$. First pass to an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$. The surjection $H\times_SU\to W$ remains surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The scheme $W_\Omega$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], normal by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], and Noetherian by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every quasi-compact open is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so the finite-component condition holds there too. Its irreducible components are disjoint integral opens by [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. In each component choose $y\in W_\Omega(\Omega)$ using [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] on that smooth open. The inverse image of $U_\Omega$ under $H_\Omega\to W_\Omega$, $g\mapsto g^{-1}y$, is nonempty by the surjection, and open. It contains an $\Omega$-point by the same density lemma. The orbit of $y$ lies in its component: it is the continuous image of the connected $H_\Omega$, and components are disjoint opens. Consequently $U_\Omega$ meets every component, and is dense in each because the component is irreducible. Hence it is dense in $W_\Omega$. The projection $W_\Omega\to W_t$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, so the image of this dense subset is dense in $W_t$. Empty fibres require no choice.

source.place: Theorem 6.8 setup: the affine open is fibrewise dense in its connected-group saturation; elementary component argument written explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-affine-boundary-cartier] to $W\to S$ and $U$. Step 2 verifies its normal affine locally Noetherian base, smooth separated finite presentation and affine-open hypotheses; step 3 verifies its fibrewise-density hypothesis. It gives the effective Cartier divisor $D=(W\setminus U)_{\mathrm{red}}$ with exactly that support. Set $L=\mathcal O_W(D)$, which is invertible by [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-properties](1). By [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] it has a global section $s$ with zero scheme $D$. Locally, if the Cartier ideal is $(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor, the dual generator trivializes $L$ and $s$ has coefficient $f$. Thus its nonvanishing open is exactly $W_s=W\setminus|D|=U$, including the empty divisor case.

source.place: Theorem 6.8 Step 1, affine case; Stacks Tag 01X0, divisors.tex lemma-characterize-OD

proof.text: Let $V$ be the union of all affine positive-power nonvanishing opens of $L$. Step 4 gives $U=W_s\subseteq V$ with exponent $1$. Since the action on $W$ is saturated, $W=H\cdot U\subseteq H\cdot V\subseteq W$. Apply [lem-sfb-connected-action-orbit-section-ampleness] to $X=W$ and this $L$. Its base and smooth separated finite-type hypotheses hold by step 2, and its saturation hypothesis is the displayed equality. It follows that $L$ is ample in the absolute sense. This produces the required invertible module without imposing connectedness of $W$, a section, or a square condition. If $U$ is empty, $W$ is empty and the same argument gives the unique line on the empty scheme, with ampleness vacuous.

source.place: Proposition 6.4(b), applied to the canonical boundary section; Theorem 6.8 affine-open case

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-5dda3887c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the new node lem-sfb-connected-action-orbit-section-ampleness and all cited statements. Guo's PDF (online only, no local copy) was read: Prop 6.4(b) p.16 assumes a normal R, a smooth flat finite-type G with connected fibres and a topologically Noetherian X of strict (N)-type, and has no Picard-admissibility hypothesis, because the proof gets a power via Prop 5.9 after component dévissage and fpqc descent. So the new node, with affine X_s, a Noetherian normal domain base and geometrically connected H, is a true specialization. It is not a duplicate: square-action-affine-orbit-criterion is Guo Cor 6.5 with the square condition, dedekind-action-boundary-ampleness is only for a Dedekind base and O(E), and group-affine-section-ampleness is the special case X=H. It is not a restatement of the item. The split follows Guo Thm 6.8 and simplifies it: D=(W\U)_red is Cartier with support W\U, so W_s=U is affine and step 5 applies 6.4(b) directly. Checked: step 1 (a smooth via the isomorphism T and smooth-restrict (c), hence open), step 2 (restricted diagonal is a base change, so W/S is fp), step 3 (density over the algebraic closure, using the disjoint normal components, rational points and connectedness of H_Omega), step 4 (boundary-cartier hypotheses, O(D) and canonical section with W_s=U). Small cases checked: U empty, U=W, trivial H. Batch-5: lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal (Stacks 056T) and lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent (Stacks 0B8W, reached via boundary-cartier) are generic scheme facts, neither given by the trace formula or Poincare duality nor steps of their proofs, so both are accepted. FIX (B3): the new node said 'geometrically connected fibres' without defining it, and def-weil-connected-scheme defines plain connectedness only. I added the item's inline definition (every field Omega over S has H_Omega connected) in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-connected-action-orbit-section-ampleness.json.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
